questions.question: Design a multi-step checkout wizard with React Router v6 and preserved state on refresh.
questions.title: Multi-Step Wizard — Router State, Persistence, and UX
questions.direct_answer:
Design a multi-step checkout wizard with React Router v6 and preserved state on refresh.

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Nested routes, URL as source of truth, persistence strategy, back/forward behavior, validation per step.

**Classic weak answer:** Storing PCI-sensitive fields in localStorage or putting secrets only in client state.

**Senior finish:** Mention **useBlocker** for unsaved changes and **transition pending UI** during navigation.

interviewer_intent.testing: Nested routes, URL as source of truth, persistence strategy, back/forward behavior, validation per step
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Storing PCI-sensitive fields in localStorage or putting secrets only in client state
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Mention **useBlocker** for unsaved changes and **transition pending UI** during navigation

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **Multi-Step Wizard — Router State, Persistence, and UX** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** Design a multi-step checkout wizard with React Router v6 and preserved state on refresh.

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **Nested routes, URL as source of truth, persistence strategy, back/forward behavior, validation per step**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Storing PCI-sensitive fields in localStorage or putting secrets only in client state**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Mention **useBlocker** for unsaved changes and **transition pending UI** during navigation**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** Nested routes, URL as source of truth, persistence strategy, back/forward behavior, validation per step
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.title: Mental model (flowchart)
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TB
    EVT[Event / state change] --> SCHED[Scheduler schedules update]
    SCHED --> DIFF[React reconciles virtual DOM]
    DIFF --> COMMIT[Commit DOM mutations]
    COMMIT --> FX[useLayoutEffect]
    COMMIT --> EF[useEffect after paint]
    subgraph Memo["Performance hooks"]
        MEMO[memo / useMemo / useCallback]
    end
    DIFF --> MEMO
```

sections.content:

| **What interviewers probe** | Nested routes, URL as source of truth, persistence strategy, back/forward behavior, validation per step |
| **Weak signal (avoid)** | Storing PCI-sensitive fields in localStorage or putting secrets only in client state |
| **Differentiator** | Mention **useBlocker** for unsaved changes and **transition pending UI** during navigation |
| **Proof you shipped it** | Metrics (LCP, error rate), tests, DevTools trace, or incident story |

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **storing PCI-sensitive fields in localStorage or putting secrets only in client state** and what you do instead.

sections.content:

- **Mechanism:** Nested routes, URL as source of truth, persistence strategy, back/forward behavior, validation per step
- **Pitfall:** Storing PCI-sensitive fields in localStorage or putting secrets only in client state
- **Differentiator:** Mention **useBlocker** for unsaved changes and **transition pending UI** during navigation
- **Proof:** DevTools / Network / Performance trace, test strategy, or metric.
- **Close:** decision rule + sensible follow-up question back to the interviewer.

sections.title: How to answer verbally (timed)
sections.content:
**Open (15–20 seconds):** Restate the question and give the one-sentence definition.

**Body (45–60 seconds):** Walk through **Nested routes, URL as source of truth, persistence strategy, back/forward behavior, validation per step** as a story: what runs, what breaks, what you log/measure.

**Pitfall (15 seconds):** Call out **Storing PCI-sensitive fields in localStorage or putting secrets only in client state** — interviewers reward honesty about real bugs.

**Finish (15–20 seconds):** Add **Mention **useBlocker** for unsaved changes and **transition pending UI** during navigation**, then offer a trade-off question back (“do you optimize for TTFB or TTI here?”).

questions.question: How do you protect a route that needs the user AND preloaded account data before render?
questions.title: Protected Routes — Loaders, Redirects, and Error Boundaries
questions.direct_answer:
How do you protect a route that needs the user AND preloaded account data before render?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Loader-based auth, redirect vs render-null flash, caching loader data, SSR considerations if any.

**Classic weak answer:** Checking auth only in `useEffect` so protected content flashes before redirect.

**Senior finish:** Note **cookie-based auth** vs `Authorization` header for SSR and CSRF implications.

interviewer_intent.testing: Loader-based auth, redirect vs render-null flash, caching loader data, SSR considerations if any
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Checking auth only in `useEffect` so protected content flashes before redirect
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Note **cookie-based auth** vs `Authorization` header for SSR and CSRF implications
